truthBoundary: This program defines the public GitHub readiness boundary for SEIS AI. It does not prove AGI, install models, download checkpoints, train a 512B model, run inference, run benchmarks, call providers, provision cloud/GPU resources, execute SSH, push, merge, deploy, publish checkpoints, or grant runtime authority.

internetResearchBaseline.seisImplication: 512B SEIS work must be treated as frontier-scale research, not as a local runtime claim.
512B training needs distributed architecture, data governance, evaluation, observability, budget, and rollback evidence.
Total parameters, active parameters, routing, memory, licensing, and evaluation must be tracked separately.
Public AI readiness needs governance, risk mapping, measurement, management, transparency, and accountability gates.
SEIS AGI and 512B readiness needs misuse, privacy, cybersecurity, transparency, and measurement gates before public claims.
AGI-style autonomy claims need time-horizon evidence, not demos, parameter count, or installed assistant presence.

githubAudienceModes.allowedUse: Run the Local Demo, inspect AI contracts, and run local validators without provider keys.
githubAudienceModes.forbiddenUse: Treat SEIS as a trained 512B model, live AGI, routeable inference service, or provider-key-backed assistant.

githubAudienceModes.allowedUse: Review PRs, run validators, inspect evidence, and record human approvals.
githubAudienceModes.forbiddenUse: Push, merge, release, deploy, publish weights, or unlock runtime authority without explicit approval and passing checks.

githubAudienceModes.allowedUse: Review public artifacts, challenge evidence, and propose benchmark or safety improvements.
githubAudienceModes.forbiddenUse: Count plan-only records as independent AGI evidence.

githubAudienceModes.allowedUse: No real AGI use is available today.
